question: What is the primary function of the lower oesophageal sphincter?

options.A: To absorb digested nutrients into the bloodstream
options.B: To help push chewed food down into the throat
options.C: To prevent stomach acid from flowing backward
options.D: To produce enzymes that break down proteins

explanation: The lower oesophageal sphincter acts as a one-way valve separating the stomach from the oesophagus to keep gastric contents down. [learn more](BMP125_U3_T3#BMP125_U3_T3_h1)

question: Why does stomach acid cause damage to the oesophagus?

options.A: The stomach secretes alkaline substances that irritate cells
options.B: Food particles trapped in the tube rub against the mucosa
options.C: Digestive enzymes inside the acid actively eat through muscle
options.D: The oesophageal lining lacks protection against harsh acid

explanation: Unlike the stomach, which has a thick protective mucus layer, the oesophagus lining is easily irritated and damaged by acidic gastric juices. [learn more](BMP125_U3_T3#BMP125_U3_T3_h1)

question: Which of the following conditions is the most common cause of oesophagitis?
explanation: GERD remains the primary driver behind inflammation of the lower oesophageal lining worldwide. [learn more](BMP125_U3_T3#BMP125_U3_T3_h2)

question: A patient takes strong capsules right before bed with only a tiny sip of water and wakes up with severe sharp pain when swallowing. What is the most likely cause?
explanation: Pills swallowed without enough fluid while lying down can stick to the oesophageal wall and cause direct localized chemical burns. [learn more](BMP125_U3_T3#BMP125_U3_T3_h2)

question: What medical term describes painful swallowing experienced by patients with oesophagitis?
explanation: Odynophagia specifically refers to pain felt during swallowing due to inflammation and ulceration along the tract. [learn more](BMP125_U3_T3#BMP125_U3_T3_h3)

question: Why do many patients with severe oesophagitis experience unintended weight loss?

options.A: The inflamed stomach completely stops absorbing any calories
options.B: High fever speeds up the body's metabolism drastically
options.C: Acid reflux causes constant vomiting of all consumed meals
options.D: Pain during swallowing makes them avoid eating enough food

explanation: When swallowing hurts or feels blocked, patients naturally cut down on food intake, leading to nutritional deficits and weight loss. [learn more](BMP125_U3_T3#BMP125_U3_T3_h3)

question: Which diagnostic procedure is considered the gold standard for viewing mucosal damage in oesophagitis?
explanation: Endoscopy allows direct visual assessment of the oesophageal lining, grading inflammation and ruling out other conditions. [learn more](BMP125_U3_T3#BMP125_U3_T3_h4)

question: What primary preparation must a midwife ensure before a patient undergoes an upper gastrointestinal endoscopy?

options.A: The patient must drink a large volume of sugary fluid
options.B: The patient must fast for a specified number of hours
options.C: The patient must take strong laxatives the night before
options.D: The patient must lie flat on their abdomen for an hour

explanation: Fasting ensures the stomach is empty, reducing the risk of aspiration and giving the doctor a clear view during the procedure. [learn more](BMP125_U3_T3#BMP125_U3_T3_h4)

question: How do proton pump inhibitors primarily work to treat oesophagitis?

options.A: By forming a physical shield over the stomach lining
options.B: By speeding up the digestion of fats in the intestines
options.C: By paralyzing the lower sphincter to keep food down
options.D: By blocking cellular mechanisms that secrete gastric acid

explanation: Proton pump inhibitors shut down the acid pumps in the stomach wall, drastically reducing the amount of acid reaching the oesophagus. [learn more](BMP125_U3_T3#BMP125_U3_T3_h5)

question: A patient with mild acid reflux needs immediate relief from a burning sensation behind the sternum. Which drug class is best suited for quick symptom reduction?
explanation: Antacids act instantly to neutralize existing stomach acid, offering quick relief for acute burning symptoms. [learn more](BMP125_U3_T3#BMP125_U3_T3_h5)

question: Why is elevating the head of the bed recommended for patients with reflux-induced oesophagitis?

options.A: It improves the lung capacity during the night hours
options.B: It speeds up the emptying of the large intestine
options.C: Gravity helps keep stomach contents down while sleeping
options.D: It prevents saliva from pooling in the back of the throat

explanation: Elevating the head uses gravity to discourage gastric acid from flowing upward into the oesophagus during sleep. [learn more](BMP125_U3_T3#BMP125_U3_T3_h6)

question: Which of the following dietary items should patients with oesophagitis NOT consume freely?
explanation: Spicy and high-fat foods relax the lower oesophageal sphincter and stimulate more acid production, worsening symptoms. [learn more](BMP125_U3_T3#BMP125_U3_T3_h6)

question: What is Barrett's oesophagus?

options.A: An abnormal widening of the lower sphincter muscle
options.B: A pre-cancerous change in the lining due to chronic acid exposure
options.C: A sudden bacterial infection causing swelling of the throat muscles
options.D: A congenital pouch forming near the upper part of the chest

explanation: Chronic cellular injury causes normal lining cells to transform into abnormal types, increasing the risk of malignancy over time. [learn more](BMP125_U3_T3#BMP125_U3_T3_h7)

question: What causes an oesophageal stricture to form in chronic inflammation?

options.A: Permanent overgrowth of the muscular wall from constant use
options.B: Continuous production of thick mucus by irritated glands
options.C: Accumulation of fibrous scar tissue from repeated healing
options.D: Deposition of undigested food particles inside the mucosal folds

explanation: As chronic ulcers heal, fibrous scar tissue contracts and narrows the internal diameter of the oesophagus, causing strictures. [learn more](BMP125_U3_T3#BMP125_U3_T3_h7)
